s.t:
OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI.

Accordingly, our Global Affairs team builds authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials and the broader AI policymaking community to inform and support our shared work in these domains.

We ensure that insights from policymakers inform our work and - in collaboration with our colleagues and external stakeholders - support the development of regulation, industry standards, and safe and beneficial development of AI tools.

As the EU Policy & Partnerships Manager, you will develop strategies, shape OpenAI’s approach to priority EU policy issues, and drive campaigns as part of our European team. You will also develop and manage relationships with key stakeholders across the Brussels policy ecosystem, including policymakers, regulators, civil society groups, industry associations, researchers and experts, seeking to advance policies and partnerships that align with OpenAI’s mission.
OpenAI releases industry-leading research and tools. You will face new challenges as the impact of cutting-edge generative AI technologies continues to be explored and as the needs of the organization evolve. Day-to-day work may encompass anything from helping to shape strategic initiatives and developing policy positions to preparing our leaders for engagements with EU officials or representing OpenAI in private and public forums.
We are looking for a self-directed and creative individual with deep EU policy expertise, experience managing relationships across the Brussels policy ecosystem, sound judgment, and a sophisticated understanding of AI and AI-related legislative and regulatory issues and processes. The ideal candidate will be able to move between strategic policy development and practical delivery, working across teams to advance OpenAI’s mission in Brussels.
This strategic yet hands-on role will report to the EU Policy & Partnerships Lead and work closely with key internal and external partners.
This role is based in our Brussels office and will involve occasional travel. We follow a hybrid work model with three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

s.h: You should thrive in this role if you
s.t:
Have deep knowledge of the EU policy ecosystem, including the institutions, legislative and regulatory processes, key debates shaping AI and technology policy, and a solid understanding of the member state policy landscape.
Are a trusted relationship builder who can engage credibly with EU officials, regulators, civil society groups, industry associations, researchers and experts across the Brussels policy ecosystem.
Can translate complex AI concepts into practical policy relevance for EU policymakers and Brussels stakeholders.
Are comfortable operating independently while collaborating closely across teams in a fast-moving environment.
Are passionate about the promise of technology and the future of artificial intelligence but thoughtful about its potential risks.

About PostHog
Product development used to mean manually writing code, running analysis, diagnosing bugs, and rolling out changes using dozens of tools.
PostHog makes products self-driving . It's the only platform that acts like a co-pilot for you (and your AI agents) to do it all – autonomously.
We started with open-source product analytics, launched out of Y Combinator's W20 cohort . We've since shipped more than a dozen products , including:
PostHog Desktop , the only AI devtool that understands your product, not just your codebase.
A built-in data warehouse , so users can query product and customer data together using custom SQL insights.
PostHog AI , an AI-powered analyst that answers product questions, helps users find useful session recordings, and writes custom SQL queries.

Product-led . More than 450,000 organizations have installed PostHog, mostly driven by word-of-mouth. We have intensely strong product-market fit.
Default alive . Revenue is growing incredibly quickly, and we're very efficient. We raise money to push ambition and grow faster, not to keep the lights on.
Well-funded. We've raised more than $180m from some of the world's top investors. We're set up for a long, ambitious journey.
We're focused on building an awesome product for end users, hiring exceptional teammates, shipping fast, and being as weird as possible .
Things we care about
Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook . Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions.
Autonomy: We don’t tell anyone what to do. Everyone chooses what to work on next based on what's going to have the biggest impact on our customers, and what they find interesting and motivating to work on. Engineers lead product teams and make product decisions . Teams are flexible and easy to change when needed.
Shipping fast: Why not now? We want to build a lot of products; we can't do that shipping at a normal pace. We've built the company around small teams – autonomous, highly-efficient groups of cracked engineers who can outship much larger companies because they own their products end-to-end.
Time for building: Nothing gets shipped in a meeting. We're a natively remote company. We default to async communication – PRs > Issues > Slack. Tuesdays and Thursdays are meeting-free days , and we prioritize heads down building time over perfect coordination. This will be the most productive job you've ever had.
Ambition: We want to solve big problems. We strongly believe that aiming for the best possible upside, and sometimes missing, is better than never trying. We're optimistic about what's possible and our ability to get there.
Being weird: Weird means redesigning an already world-class website for the 5th time. It means shipping literally every product that relates to customer data. It means building an objectively unnecessary developer toy with dubious shareholder value. Doing weird stuff is a competitive advantage. And it's fun.
Why this role? Why now?
PostHog is building every product companies need to run their business – and more than 100,000 companies have already installed us, mostly through word of mouth. Now we're ready to go find the ones who don't know about us yet. This role is the architect of that motion.
You'll help build and scale our playbook – from targeting logic to tooling stack to coaching cadence to disqualification criteria. You'll have a small, high-potential team, a product that engineers love, transparent pricing that makes outbound easier (not harder), and a set of sales leaders who care more about pipeline quality than activity volume.
If you've been frustrated by BDR orgs that optimize for dials-per-day and ignore whether the meetings are any good, this is the opposite of that. We want the pipeline and we want to not ruin our brand.

PostHog's brand is a true advantage – prospects have often heard of us or used the free tier. Cold outreach here is warmer than most.
The New Business Sales team has a strong track record. Your pipeline will be worked by experienced, technical AEs who know how to close.
We value learning, being creative and standing out in the market more than a playbook you've done a thousand times.
PostHog's culture is async, remote-first, and low-meeting. You'll spend your time building and coaching, not sitting in standups.

1–2+ years managing or formally leading a BDR/SDR team as a player-coach, with direct responsibility for hiring, coaching, and performance management. "Team lead" with informal authority counts if you can demonstrate coaching impact on rep performance. We are structured for speed and autonomy , so your leadership style needs to fit our model. This is less command & control, and more set context, build systems, coach selectively & judge on outputs.
Prior individual quota-carrying experience. You've personally prospected, booked meetings, and ideally closed deals. You know what good looks like because you've done it, not just managed it. You’ll do it again here.
Demonstrated ability to think in data, systems, and loops – even at a smaller scale. You know how to build the operating system the team runs on. You've designed or significantly improved a prospecting workflow, built reporting from scratch, or created a repeatable process where one didn't exist before.
Hands-on experience with Clay.com . You've built tables, enrichment workflows, and automated sequences in Clay – not just used outputs someone else created. If you can show us a Clay workflow you designed, that's a strong signal.
Salesforce proficiency. You can build reports, create custom fields, manage lead/contact data hygiene, and don't need someone else to configure your CRM.
AI-capable, with experience building automation. You've used AI tools (LLMs, AI writing assistants, workflow automation) to improve prospecting efficiency. You should be able to articulate specific examples: "I built X using Y and it improved Z by W%."
Excellent written communication. Your outreach sequences, coaching notes, and Slack messages are clear, concise, and sharp. PostHog is an async-first company – writing quality matters.
Comfort with ambiguity and distributed ownership. This is a build role, not a maintain role. You'll be handed a rough playbook and expected to own it with your team, and you’ll have a company full of drivers who will give you “yes, and…” feedback

Experience in a product-led sales (PLS) or product-led growth (PLG) company where the buyer often starts with a free/self-serve tier before engaging sales.
Familiarity with selling to engineers and engineering managers as the primary buyer persona.
Experience with PostHog or competing products as a user or seller.
What You’ll Be Doing
Own the outbound pipeline engine. Iterate on the targeting strategy, account selection criteria, and signal-based prioritization that tells your team who to reach and why now. Start with what doesn't scale, then systematize it.

Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. Meet every member of the BDR team and all key stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, and RevOps. Understand the current state of pipeline generation, rep productivity, and tool stack. Audit existing processes, sequencing, and messaging. Identify the most urgent gaps and the highest-leverage opportunities to improve performance fast.

The playbook is live and being executed consistently across regions. Ramp programs are in place for new hires. Pipeline generation is trending toward targets. About One Acre Fund
Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services.

On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

By 2030, our organisation will serve 10 million farm families annually. This growth will be fuelled by fundraising, and at One Acre Fund, our fundraising relies on industry-leading grant and partnership management. We have a 10-person grant management team within our larger Business Development department, responsible for stewarding our highest-value donor partnerships, and are now looking for new Strategic Partnerships Senior Associates / Managers to join this team.
These roles will manage some of our highest-value donor partnerships, leading the coordination and monitoring of grant-funded activities. All roles will report to leaders within our Global Business Development team, while closely coordinating with leaders for the relevant programs.

All roles will also interact closely across 1AF’s programming, building deep fluency with our approach to smallholder agriculture: equipping farmers with high-quality products/services to increase their harvests and profits, build their climate resilience, and improve their long-term livelihoods.
Specific roles will have major emphasis areas based on the nature of each donor partnership, helping the organisation pioneer new approaches to thematic priorities including conservation agriculture, engaging women and youth farmers, and smallholder insurance.

Drive thematic partnerships happening in the field: You will bring an ambitious vision of smallholder prosperity to life in new thematic areas for the organisation, helping us build the capacity to deliver impact to smallholders through conservation agriculture, women/youth engagement, and/or smallholder insurance:
Project Management and Coordination: Partner with program teams to set goals, design and run project activities, anticipate challenges, and keep every part of the plan moving forward smoothly.
Collaborative Problem Solving: Work closely with program staff to tackle day-to-day and long-term challenges, bringing real-world insights directly to org leadership and the donor.
Program Fluency: Spend dedicated time in the field with farmers and staff to fully understand work and ensure that all we do in the partnership remains tailored to what farmers really need.
Own, manage and/or support key donor relationships: You will ensure One Acre Fund builds and maintains an excellent relationship with our partners, translating field impact into clear, compelling narratives and keeping our partners deeply connected to our progress:
Donor Engagement: Act as the main point of contact for all funder communications, seamlessly bridging the gap between donors and field teams in whatever ways are needed, including regular communications, coordinating visits, and more as required.
Storytelling and Reporting: Through deep program fluency, deliver clear, high-quality narrative and financial updates that demonstrate to our partners the true impact of their support.
Grant Administration: Manage the essential day-to-day details of the funding, including accurate data tracking, invoices, and otherwise ensuring all grant operations are running smoothly and on time.

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. Every business grows through a CRM and a direct line to its customers. Healthcare, and pharmacy most of all, is the one place that never happened. It was too hard to build, too hard to distribute, and too hard to do compliantly. Customer data sits idle whilst running a community healthcare business continues to become structurally tighter.
We're on a mission to change that. We are the compliant data layer for community healthcare: the system that lets a pharmacy use the patient data it already holds to grow revenue and relationships, compliantly, on the clinical system it already runs.
This is already working. Pharmlogic is NHS-assured, integrated and lives in hundreds of pharmacies nationwide, and we've powered millions of patient communications.

s.h: The role as Pharmacy Partnerships Manager
s.t:
This is a senior sales hire and it carries real ownership. You will run the full sales cycle for pharmacy accounts across the UK, from first conversation to signed customer, and you will set the standard for how Pharmlogic sells. As we grow, you help shape the team that grows around you, and we all hold each other to a high standard.
You report to the CEO and work closely with the founding team. This is a consultative, relationship-led sale into pharmacy owners and groups, won on trust and domain credibility rather than pressure. It suits a full-cycle seller who sources their own pipeline, works without close supervision, and wants to own a function rather than work a list of tasks.
Some of the problems you'll be solving

s.h: As Pharmacy Partnerships Manager, you'll be
s.t:
Building the engine, not just closing deals: Designing and scaling the sales system that takes Pharmlogic from hundreds of pharmacies to thousands. You own the pipeline and the machine that generates it.
Finding the providers ready to grow: Using data intelligently to focus on the pharmacies who stand to gain most from Pharmlogic, independents and multiples alike, and building a repeatable way to reach them at scale.
Selling consultatively, winning on trust: Leading discovery and demonstrations with owners, superintendents and group decision-makers, earning the credibility a healthcare sale is won on.
Owning the number: Carrying a personal revenue target and running your deals end to end, with the autonomy to close them your way.
Setting customers up to win: Owning the handover to onboarding so every pharmacy starts strong and gets full value from day one.
Sharpening how we all sell: Bringing the market back into the room, from events, owners and data, so the whole team gets sharper together, from targeting to pitch to product.
This could be for you, if
You're proven: You've carried a revenue target and hit it, consistently. You're a closer with a track record, not someone who needs the machine built around them first.
You can coach, not just sell: You've mentored or led salespeople and you get energy from making others better. As we grow, the team forms around you, and you're the standard they learn from.
You are fast. Genuinely fast: You move at a pace most people find hard to keep up with. You reply, follow up, and close while others are still planning. Speed is your edge and you know it.
You're fluent with a CRM: You run your pipeline in the tools, not in your head. Clean data, accurate stages, no deal slipping through a crack.
You can forecast: You set targets and call your number with confidence, and you're usually right. You bring commercial clarity, not optimism dressed as a pipeline.
You thrive on pace and ownership: You have a driver's mindset, urgent and resourceful, and you build repeatable things in a fast-moving company rather than waiting for one to exist.
You know the NHS: Experience selling into the NHS or primary care is a strong advantage. Pharmacy specifically is close to ideal. Not essential if everything above is true, but it's a real head start.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

We're seeking a senior business development leader to own Anthropic's BD partnership footprint with a small number of the world's largest and most consequential technology companies. These are not single-threaded accounts.

Each relationship spans many businesses at once — consumer products, devices and operating systems, productivity and collaboration software, cloud and developer platforms, commerce, and enterprise distribution. Your job is to see the whole board, decide where Anthropic should lean in and where it shouldn't, and turn that judgment into signed deals.
The center of gravity for this role is product and distribution partnerships: co-developing opportunities with partners, and structuring the commercial, technical, and go-to-market terms that make those partnerships durable. You'll typically be running several deal streams inside the same partner in parallel — at different stages, with different counterparts, and with terms that interact with one another — and you'll be the person responsible for keeping them coherent.
This is an individual contributor role for a seasoned dealmaker who is comfortable as the primary counterpart to senior executives at very large companies, who brings strong judgment to ambiguous, high-stakes situations, and who can carry a complex, multi-party negotiation from first conversation through signature and into execution.

Manage a small number of large, multi-faceted partner relationships end to end: set the strategy for each relationship, decide which opportunities to pursue and in what order, and stay accountable for the overall health and commercial output of the partnership across every surface it touches
Lead product partnerships: identify and structure opportunities to embed Claude in partners' consumer and enterprise products, co-develop new products and features, and define the product, technical, data, and brand terms that come with them, working closely with Anthropic's product and engineering leaders
Run multiple deal streams in parallel: manage several concurrent negotiations within the same partner — product integrations, distribution and go-to-market, commercial and consumption agreements, and infrastructure — and sequence and connect them so terms in one stream reinforce rather than undercut the others
Negotiate complex, first-of-kind agreements: lead end-to-end negotiations involving novel commercial structures, revenue and economics sharing, product and roadmap commitments, exclusivity and competitive provisions, data terms, and multi-year, multi-component value exchanges
Act as an executive counterpart: build and manage relationships with senior executives and their teams on the partner side, serve as Anthropic's primary voice into the partnership, and prepare and steer Anthropic's own executives through partner-level engagements
Exercise judgment on behalf of Anthropic: weigh commercial upside against strategic, competitive, product, and mission considerations; know when to say no; and make clear, well-reasoned recommendations to Anthropic leadership on trade-offs that don't have a playbook
Drive cross-functional execution: coordinate Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Legal, and Policy across the life of a partnership, from initial structuring through negotiation, launch, and ongoing governance, ensuring what we sign is something Anthropic can deliver

About Cult Beauty
Cult Beauty is one of the UK's leading online beauty destinations, known for a curated, expert-led edit of the best emerging and established beauty brands. As part of THG, Cult Beauty combines an entrepreneurial, fast-moving culture with the scale, data and technology of a global e-commerce group.

The affiliates and partnerships channel is a genuine growth priority for the business, with strong performance to date and significant headroom to scale reach, revenue and brand awareness over the next 12–24 months.
Why be a Senior Affiliates & Partnerships Manager at THG Beauty?
We're looking for a Senior Affiliates & Partnerships Manager to take ownership of Cult Beauty's affiliate channel and lead its next phase of growth. This is a hands-on role; you'll set the strategy and own the numbers. You will also be in the detail, planning activations, negotiating placements, managing budgets in real time, and reporting on performance. It suits someone who is equally comfortable building a forecast model as they are briefing a publisher or optimising a live campaign.
You'll own the channel's budget end-to-end, from annual and quarterly planning and forecasting through to in-month tracking, reforecasting and reconciliation against actuals, while also executing the campaigns and activations that bring the strategy to life.

You'll use data, including media mix modelling (MMM) and other cross-channel measurement, to understand the channel's true incremental contribution and its role in the wider marketing mix, and you'll look for opportunities for the channel to support broader brand awareness goals, not just direct performance.

s.h: As Senior Affiliates & Partnerships Manager you’ll
s.t:
Channel strategy & scale
Own the affiliate and partnerships strategy for Cult Beauty, identifying and prioritising the highest-value opportunities to scale reach, revenue and new customer acquisition.
Build the channel out from its current base, expanding the partner mix across content, cashback, loyalty, influencer-affiliate and technology partners, while protecting margin and brand value.
Identify and develop opportunities for the channel to support wider brand awareness objectives, working with brand and content teams to use partnerships (e.g. content, video and influencer-affiliate placements) to build reach and consideration alongside direct performance.
Keep the channel's commercial model, commission structure and partner tiering under continuous review, benchmarking against market practice.
Budget planning, forecasting & management
Lead annual and quarterly budget planning and revenue/commission forecasting for the channel, working closely with finance and the wider marketing leadership team.
Own in-month budget management and pacing, tracking spend and commission against forecast, reforecasting as needed, and flagging variances before they become a problem.
Build and maintain robust forecasting models that link activity, seasonality and commercial terms to expected return, and use these to make the case for investment.
Apply media mix modelling (MMM) outputs and other cross-channel measurement to inform budget allocation, understand the channel's incremental contribution, and stress-test planning assumptions against the wider marketing mix.
Reconcile monthly performance against budget and finance records, ensuring accurate, timely reporting on channel P&L.
Activation execution & campaign management
Plan and execute the affiliate activation calendar, from always-on placements through to peak trading moments (e.g. Black Friday, Cyber Monday, key beauty launches) and brand awareness activity.
Brief, negotiate and manage relationships with affiliate networks, publishers, content creators and technology partners to secure high-quality, cost-effective placements.
Own day-to-day channel operations: commission structuring, tracking and validation, compliance, and troubleshooting technical or performance issues.
Use AI-driven tools and optimization, for example automated bid/commission optimisation, AI-assisted content, creative or audience targeting to improve campaign efficiency and free up time for strategic activity.
Data, insight & reporting
Use data to drive decisions across the channel, analysing performance by partner, placement and campaign to identify what's working and reallocate budget accordingly.
Own regular and ad hoc reporting for senior stakeholders, translating channel performance into clear commercial insight and recommendations.
Partner with wider analytics/BI teams to improve attribution, measurement and incrementality understanding for the channel.
Leadership & collaboration
Lead, coach and develop the affiliates team, setting clear priorities and creating capacity to scale as the channel grows.
Act as the primary point of contact for the affiliates channel with cross-functional teams, including brand, finance and commercial, ensuring alignment on priorities and investment.
Collaborate closely with other marketing channels, including paid social, PR, influencer and CRM to align messaging, avoid duplication of partner relationships, and ensure affiliate activity is planned as part of an integrated, cross-channel marketing calendar.
Represent Cult Beauty externally with networks, agencies and partners, building a reputation as a commercially sharp, collaborative partner.

s.h: What skills and experience do I need for this role?
s.t:
Proven experience managing an affiliate/partnerships channel in a fast-paced e-commerce, retail or beauty environment, ideally at Manager level or above already.
Strong data acumen: confident building and interrogating models in Excel/Google Sheets, comfortable working across GA4/BI tools and media mix modelling (MMM) or cross-channel measurement outputs, and able to translate data into a clear commercial story.
Demonstrable experience owning a budget end-to-end: annual/quarterly planning and forecasting through to in-month management, pacing and reconciliation with finance.

You are the first human a London landlord speaks to. We generate the demand — paid inbound, portal activity, lead ads pre-qualified by our own AI agent, cold email, leaflets, referrals — and you turn it into signed instructions.
Landlords rarely arrive asking for a named product; they arrive with a problem — an agent they've had enough of, a property they can't get to, a tenancy they don't want to run. Your first job is to work out which of our services solves it, and say so. Valuations, viewings, photography and key handovers sit with operations, so your day is conversations, offers and closes.
This is one role across four rungs, levelled on the scope you own rather than years served. At BDC you work the company lead feeds from the desk: qualify, put a number in front of the landlord, close instructions across the range. At Senior BDC you take the harder pipeline — portfolios, agent switches, the deals that need pricing judgement.

At BDM you own the close, the price and the commercials, with your own sourcing on top of the feeds. At Senior BDM you carry the largest number and own retention.
What you'll own
The first call. Every new lead lands as a task with your name on it. You call it the day it lands, and you get to the landlord's real constraint — money, distance or hassle — before you pitch anything.
The routing decision. DIY, Placed, Managed or Secured — you decide which tier fits the property and the landlord, and you answer for the ones routed wrong.
The number. A figure is the hook; a brochure isn't. You give the landlord what they'd achieve and what they'd take home on each route — and you answer the two objections that lose deals on the same call: price (net income across the whole term, not a headline rent) and trust ("is this rent-to-rent", "will I get my property back" — answered from the agreement).
Your pipeline, in the CRM. Outcome logged, lead status set, next step dated — before you finish the call. A lead with no next step is a lead we've lost.
The close and the price. First conversation → assessment → offer → signed agreement, without being chased through it, then the renter offers that decide what the property actually lets for. You recommend the figure and defend it, knowing the company lives with it for the full term.
The commercials, and your own sourcing. Fee, term and let price on a Managed instruction; the spread on a Secured one. You answer for what the deal earns, not just that it closed. Company feeds are a floor: portfolio landlords, agent switches and referrers you build yourself sit on top.
Senior BDM: retention. Re-signing a landlord is worth more than finding a new one. You own the renewal number and the save.
How we sell
We sell the outcome, not the product. Rent that arrives, a tenancy that runs itself, compliance that never lands on the landlord — then route to the tier that delivers it and price it properly.
We're honest — about the trade and about what we're on the hook for. Every tier asks something of the landlord and gives something back. No subletting, no company lets, no short lets; the landlord stays the landlord. Said plainly, that wins more than overselling — and filters out the price-shoppers who are our biggest single loss reason.
We price on evidence. Comparables, condition, void risk and the renter market decide the figure — not how badly you want the instruction — and nothing gets promised that the valuation won't support.
AI does the prep, you do the selling. Property and market research, call notes, follow-up drafts and pipeline hygiene are increasingly automated. We expect you to use that, not to type around it.

Experience.
BDC: ~1-2 years in a target-driven, phone-led sales role.
BDM / Senior BDM: ~2+ years closing your own deals — consistently at or above quota, with a number you can evidence.
Lettings or BTR instruction-winning strongly preferred; estate agency or another consultative, high-volume sales background considered.
Grit and a desire to win. You make the last call of the day sound like the first, and a bad week makes you dial more, not less.
You run your own pipeline properly — dated next steps, clean CRM, nothing dropped — and you can cold-call without warming up first.
Current lettings market and the regulation around it, including what the Renters' Rights Act changed for voids, notices and renewals, or you can learn it inside a month.
BDC: you can work a company lead feed at volume and handle a "no" in one move.
Senior BDC: a record of closing in a complex, priced product, and of lifting the reps around you.
BDM: commercial judgement on price — you can hold a figure, walk away from a bad one, and explain both — and you self-source: given a patch and a phone, you build pipeline.
Senior BDM: you've carried the largest number on a desk and owned renewals or retention.

Guaranteed rent, rent-to-rent or corporate lettings — including knowing why we're structured differently.
Portfolio landlord, block or relocation-agency relationships in London.
HubSpot, or another CRM you ran properly rather than tolerated, and comfort with your own reporting.
Being early on a desk that then scaled.
Who does well here
You want to win. You count your own numbers, you know where you sit on the desk, and being behind bothers you until it isn't true any more.
You call. The best rep here isn't the most articulate one, it's the one who dials.
You'd rather lose fast than write a bad deal. A maybe you nurse costs a week; a mispriced property is a multi-year problem.
You protect the margin as if it were yours, on the landlord side and the renter side.
Why apply
You'll be a critical human in an AI-Native company optimised for efficiency. We believe homes will be run more efficiently and at a higher quality for customers with AI, and we're building the platform that will run all rental properties end-to-end, starting with London.
We've raised a $4m pre-seed from investors who've built the financial and operational infrastructure that moves billions and serves millions. They backed us because the home is the largest consumer asset where that infrastructure hasn't been built yet. You'll get competitive base pay, meaningful equity, and a small, high-agency team rebuilding an industry and growing at >100% month-over-month. We're hiring to facilitate this aggressive growth.
Bonus is uncapped. Hit target and you take home your OTE; beat it and there is no ceiling.

The ability to work independently without day-to-day direction, while remaining a strong and collaborative team player.
Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles and closing high-value commercial agreements.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and relationship management skills.

Are customer-centric. You are motivated to deeply understand your customer’s priorities and help them achieve their vision for using our models to improve their products and services. You build strong relationships with executives and professionals across functions and serve as a trusted advisor.
Have a passion or deep curiosity in artificial intelligence. You embrace the opportunity to help deploy our technology in a way that benefits humanity. You’re excited to educate our customers on AI and how to plan for the future.
Are a builder. You are excited to impact how our company operates and scales. Your passion is building strong systems and processes from the ground up and executing them with precision.
Are excited by new challenges. You don’t have the answers to every question up front, but the process of solving them invigorates you. Bespoke issues requiring multidimensional knowledge excite you. You’re willing to experiment with new solutions.
Are a strategist. You deeply understand go to market best practices and raise the bar for our organization. You think and plan forward on the order of years and bring internal and external stakeholders along with your strategy.
About OpenAI
OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products.

AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.
We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.
For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement .
Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates.

For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information.

In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About Beneficial Deployments
Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences. We prioritize opportunities to make AI more accessible and raise the floor of what is possible in a given domain while also partnering with leaders to help expand the use of AI to new tasks that raise the ceiling of what is possible.

We're looking for a Partnership Manager to grow our AI for Science Program . You'll build and manage partnerships with individual labs from around the world. This program is the primary way that Anthropic’s life sciences efforts work with individual labs that have new and innovative ideas for how Claude can contribute to a growing set of scientific domains.
In this role, you'll help build our approach to deploying Claude for Life Sciences across domains of research including the biomedical sciences, chemistry, and materials science. You'll work with incredibly interdisciplinary partners from academia as well as early stage companies.

Your goal will be to develop relationships and goal directed partnerships that demonstrate or expand the capabilities of Claude in the sciences. You will focus both on individual projects but also building communities of practice that bring together scientists with similar interests or objectives.

The right person will combine genuine curiosity and grounding in the sciences with an entrepreneurial and experimental drive to build something new at the frontier of AI.

Execute Anthropic's AI for Science API credit program, managing day-to-day partnerships with academic labs, small start-ups, and potentially foundations
Identify, evaluate, and onboard new partners via our API credit application calls as well as targeted relationship building
Serve as the primary relationship owner for AI for Science, coordinating with Anthropic’s Applied AI, product, and GTM teams to deliver impact
Compile regular reports and learnings from the AI for Science ecosystem to help inform research and GTM priorities
Manage timelines, resource requirements, and regular reporting associated with the AI for Science program
Work closely with partners to understand their technical and operational needs and translate them into deployment plans
Comfort with early technical prototyping and testing to help learn alongside and unblock partners
Contribute to a research agenda for understanding AI's impact on individual labs across domains
Identify opportunities to create public goods -- open-source tools, datasets, and research -- that benefit the broader ecosystem
Represent Anthropic at global scientific convenings and conferences
Help shape team processes and culture as we scale our Life Science work

A growing network in the life sciences: you understand the landscape of universities, research institutes, and tools companies, and are energized by building new relationships

Business Development Representative (BDR)
At Klaviyo, our mission is to help businesses own their growth . We empower creators, entrepreneurs, and e-commerce brands to build meaningful relationships with their customers through powerful data, automation, and marketing tools. As a Business Development Representative (BDR), you’ll be a key part of bringing that mission to life—introducing eCommerce brands to the Klaviyo platform, setting the foundation for long-term success.
BDRs take a proactive approach—researching and reaching out to brands who haven’t yet engaged with us. You’ll build a pipeline through cold outreach, strategic prospecting, and compelling messaging. This track requires grit, creativity, and resilience to open doors and create new opportunities.
How You’ll Make an Impact
Generate qualified opportunities for the sales team(Account Executive’s) through a rigorous qualification approach
Build prospective relationships with e-commerce brands and help them understand how Klaviyo can drive their growth.
Learn to effectively identify buyer needs, position Klaviyo’s value, and route leads appropriately to Account Executives.
Stay organized, focused, and consistent in your outreach across multiple channels—calls, emails, and social.
Demonstrate grit and resilience by staying positive and motivated, even in the face of rejection.
Reflect Klaviyo’s core values of accountability, effort, and winning as one in every interaction.
Share insights, contribute to a supportive team culture, and help improve our processes as we scale.
Transform workflows by putting AI at the center, building smarter systems and ways of working from the ground up.

Driven by a strong desire to launch a career in tech sales, with ambitions to grow into roles like Account Executive.
Possess grit, resilience, and curiosity —you bounce back quickly and always want to learn more.
Thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments with high standards and clear goals.
A strong communicator who’s confident over the phone, clear in writing, and thoughtful in your approach.
Self-motivated, coachable, and energized by being part of a high-performing team.
Fluency in English and Mandarin s required.
You’ve already experimented with AI in work or personal projects, and you’re excited to dive in and learn fast. You’re hungry to responsibly explore new AI tools and workflows, finding ways to make your work smarter and more efficient

Klaviyo in Singapore
We are starting small but have big plans for Klaviyo in Singapore. We began expanding into Singapore in 2025, building on the strong foundation established by our APAC presence. As we grow, we are focused on developing our go-to-market teams.

As the team grows, we will continue to expand Klaviyo’s customer base in the region while building a fantastic working culture that reflects Klaviyo’s global values, alongside a strong local identity within our Singapore-based team. This is a unique opportunity to join us at an early stage and help shape the future of Klaviyo in Singapore.
One of our values as a company is Always Learning , and that mindset is strongly felt in Singapore. People are eager to grow and develop, and Klaviyo provides a great platform to support that journey. As we are still relatively early in our expansion in Singapore, there is significant headroom to grow and develop within your role—we are looking for the leaders of the future.

Your mission Everyone's talking about AI. We decide how it actually gets used across the company.
A $400 billion market. A profitable scale-up rethinking it with AI and a global freelance network. And in the middle of it, a team that doesn't primarily write code - it decides what AI should actually deliver: for more than 25,000 Talents in over 70 countries, through automation and smarter processes.
We're looking for you as a Working Student (f/m/d) Strategy & Business Development for our cross-functional strategic taskforce, based at our headquarters in Munich-Schwabing. You'll work at the intersection of strategy, business and AI - as a sparring partner for AI engineers, product and operations experts, and a former BCG consultant. Not as another engineer on the team, but as the person who makes sure the team builds the right thing.
This isn't a typical working student role for techies. You'll structure problems, build business cases, evaluate AI applications from a business perspective, and translate between what's technically possible and what's strategically right. The concepts you work on don't end up in a drawer - they get prototyped, discussed, and feed directly into our leadership team's decisions.
What You'll Actually Do AI strategy, not AI code: You'll work on strategic AI initiatives like our Talent Assistant or AutoQA 2.0 (AI-based voice file analysis) - not as a developer, but as someone who structures requirements, sets priorities, and turns early ideas into solid feature concepts. Our AI engineers handle the technical build; you make sure they're building the right thing.
Ideas become decisions: You'll analyze complex questions, build business cases using classic case logic, and develop decision-making material for our leadership team. Your analysis directly influences which AI initiatives get greenlit.
AI needs structure: Large language models are only as good as the data behind them. You'll define competency frameworks and evaluation logic that make our AI systems smarter - the content logic, not the technical implementation.
Your own projects, real ownership: You'll independently own topics from first analysis to first concept - a new AI use case, a workflow that's still manual today, an automation, a new approach. The content changes; the standard doesn't. You get responsibility, not just tasks.
Working where the leverage is highest: You'll support the team wherever the most interesting strategic questions are emerging right now. That means variety, high speed, and visible impact.
Why This Role Will Accelerate Your Growth
Here, you won't learn to code - you'll learn how to evaluate AI investments, build business cases that hold up in front of leadership, and structure complex topics so they turn into measurable business impact. It's the exact craft you'll later need in strategy consulting or corporate strategy - except here, the recommendation actually gets implemented instead of ending up in a slide deck.
You'll work closely with a former BCG consultant, AI engineers, and product experts, moving daily between strategy, business judgment, and AI.
Our last working student in this role went on to join us as a trainee - not because we promise it, but because she'd already taken on real responsibility during her time with us.
Your skillset Academic background: You're currently pursuing a Master's degree (business administration, economics, industrial engineering, or comparable) and already bring some practical experience - ideally with a strategic or analytical focus.
AI-savvy, not an AI engineer: You don't need to code or build models. But you use AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT as a power user for research, analysis, and structuring - and you understand how AI changes business processes. More important than deep technical knowledge: you can identify what problem an AI use case is actually meant to solve.
Skills: You structure complex issues cleanly and are confident enough in PowerPoint and Excel to put together compelling management presentations and business cases.
Mindset: You don't wait for someone to explain the next step. You dig into new topics on your own, think entrepreneurially, and want to develop solutions rather than just work through tasks.
Language skills: You communicate and present fluently in German and English, and naturally bring a healthy sense of humor.
Availability: You have 16–20 hours per week during the semester to work on-site at our Munich headquarters, with flexible scaling up to full-time during semester breaks.
Your winning deal Your opportunity: From day one, you'll contribute to one of the company's most strategic AI initiatives and help build solutions that improve the daily work of thousands of people.
Your mentor: Work closely with a former BCG consultant who will coach, challenge, and support your development.
Your network: Collaborate every day with AI Engineers, Product, Strategy, and Operations experts - exposure that's rarely found in traditional working student roles.
Your future: A full-time Trainee position after graduation is explicitly possible and has already become reality several times within our team.
Your benefits: Enjoy weekly pizza and snacks at the office, a lunch allowance (€ 6.90 x 4 per month), subsidized Wellpass membership, discounts through Corporate Benefits, and fantastic team and company events.
Your workplace: A flexible hybrid working model in one of our modern, dog-friendly offices.
Your impact: Join a profitable company where you'll have the freedom and trust to shape meaningful initiatives while helping build the future of work.
Our culture: An open, authentic environment and a high-performing, humorous team that looks forward to making bold decisions and exploring new ideas together.

This role is ideal for a self-starter who is comfortable working a structured pipeline, enjoys the details of good data hygiene, and has been testing how AI-powered tools can make prospecting sharper and more efficient.

As a Business Development Representative ( BDR ), you will help drive Cloudbeds’ growth by identifying, engaging, and qualifying independent hotels, boutique properties, and hospitality groups. About Wayflyer
Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The challenge
We're growing our outbound pipeline fast, and Sydney needs a leader to shape where that growth goes next. You'll take our BDR team and sharpen it into a function that doesn't just hit quota, it changes how the sales org thinks about pipeline generation.
What you'll actually do
You'll lead our outbound BDR team in Sydney, setting the strategy that keeps us ahead of the competition and raises the bar on what the function can do. Day-to-day, that means:
Turning sales-qualified leads into real pipeline opportunities, consistently
Coaching your team until they can articulate our value proposition better than anyone else in the market
Keeping the team motivated and on track to exceed monthly targets
Acting as the connective tissue between BDR and AE units, so handoffs are seamless instead of a source of friction
Partnering with Enablement on onboarding and training, so new joiners ramp fast and stay sharp
Spotting opportunities to improve sales operations and working with executive leadership to act on them
What this role could turn into
This isn't a lane, it's a launchpad. As we grow into new markets, this role is a genuine route into senior sales leadership, more scope, bigger decisions, and a direct hand in shaping where the business goes next. How far you take it is up to you.
Who thrives here
You lead with people first. You know a target is only ever hit by a team that feels genuinely backed, so you bring the emotional intelligence to motivate, coach and keep your best people engaged, not just managed.

You're analytical to your core, comfortable using data to make calls rather than relying on gut feel, but you never lose sight of the human on the other end of the decision. You've been in the trenches of a fast-paced startup or scale-up before, and you came out the other side wanting more of it, not less.
We hire for range
We're less interested in your years of experience and more interested in your trajectory. You've led outbound sales teams before and you've got the results to prove it, both as an individual contributor and as a manager. You've exceeded targets consistently, and you've got exposure to Solution Selling and/or MEDDICC. If your career so far has been a steady climb rather than a straight line, that's exactly the shape we're looking for.
Location and working policy
📍Sydney, Hybrid (3-4 days a week)
The good stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and a pension. Equity - because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

Guided by Savista ’s values of Commitment, Authenticity, Respect and Excellence (CARE), this is an exciting opportunity to join a growing team that is expanding its impact, delivering meaningful results for clients, and helping shape the future of revenue cycle performance across healthcare.

As an SDR, you'll be the first point of contact for prospective clients, introducing healthcare organizations to Savista 's innovative Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) solutions. You'll play a key role in generating qualified sales opportunities by engaging decision-makers, uncovering business needs, and scheduling meetings for our sales team.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys a fast-paced environment, is motivated by achieving goals, and wants to build a career in healthcare technology and sales. You'll receive the tools, training, and support needed to develop your sales skills while making a direct impact on our company's growth.

Research target accounts to better understand their business and identify opportunities to add value.
Create Sales Opportunities

Schedule meetings and product introductions for our sales team, helping move opportunities into the sales pipeline.

Continuously improve your prospecting, communication, and relationship-building skills through coaching and hands-on experience.

Track progress toward activity and meeting goals while maintainingaccurate CRM records.

Delivering a positive, professional experience for every prospective client you engage.

**Description de l'entreprise**
**Développez une prestation à forte valeur ajoutée mesurable pour nos clients**
Pour le compte d'un acteur majeur des services de personnel en Suisse, nous recherchons une personnalité expérimentée, dotée d'un fort esprit entrepreneurial, afin de développer, positionner et faire évoluer le **Case Management** en tant que prestation stratégique.
Vous combinez une solide expertise en Case Management avec une forte orientation client, d'excellentes compétences en conseil et un réel sens commercial.
**Description du poste**
**Votre mission**
Vous développez le Case Management pour en faire une prestation impactante et à valeur ajoutée
Vous accompagnez l'ensemble du processus, depuis l'analyse des besoins jusqu'à l'implémentation chez le client, en passant par le développement et la présentation d'une solution adaptée.
Vous assurez l'interface professionnelle entre les clients, les interlocuteurs internes et les prestataires externes, tout en veillant à la qualité des prestations, à leur efficacité et à la valeur ajoutée apportée au client.
**Vos responsabilités**
* Développer et faire évoluer l'offre de services dans le domaine du Case Management
* Positionner et promouvoir activement cette prestation auprès des clients existants et de nouveaux clients
* Identifier les besoins des clients et les opportunités commerciales dans les domaines du Case Management, de la gestion des absences, de la réintégration et de la prévention
* Conseiller les décideurs et responsables RH sur des solutions efficaces en matière d'absences liées à la santé
* Concevoir et présenter des solutions et des modèles de prestations adaptés aux besoins spécifiques des clients
* Acquérir de nouveaux mandats et accompagner les clients depuis le premier entretien jusqu'à l'implémentation de la solution
* Soutenir les responsables de clientèle internes grâce à une expertise métier solide et à des arguments commerciaux ciblés
* Coordonner et piloter la collaboration avec des prestataires externes spécialisés
* Analyser les indicateurs pertinents et développer des KPI permettant de mesurer l'efficacité des mesures ainsi que la valeur ajoutée pour les clients
* Démontrer la valeur économique générée par la réduction des absences, la diminution de la durée des cas et l'évolution positive des coûts liés aux sinistres
**Profil recherché**
**Votre profil**
Vous disposez d'une solide expérience dans le **Case Management, la gestion des absences, la gestion de la santé en entreprise**
Vous avez également une forte **orientation commerciale et client**. Vous appréciez le contact avec les clients, savez comprendre leurs besoins et êtes capable de transformer des problématiques métier en solutions convaincantes et en opportunités commerciales.
Idéalement, vous disposez des compétences et expériences suivantes :
* Plusieurs années d'expérience en Suisse dans le Case Management, les assurances, la gestion de la santé en entreprise (GSE/BGM)
* Excellentes compétences en conseil et en vente
* Expérience dans le Business Development ou le développement de prestations B2B
* Très bonne compréhension du système suisse des assurances sociales et privées
* Capacité à communiquer d'égal à égal avec les responsables RH, les directions d'entreprise et d'autres décideurs
* Esprit entrepreneurial et excellente capacité à identifier les besoins des clients et les potentiels du marché
* Formation supérieure dans les domaines de la santé, des assurances, des ressources humaines, du travail social ou dans un domaine comparable ; une formation complémentaire en Case Management constitue un atout
* Très bonnes connaissances de l'allemand et du français ; l'anglais constitue un atout (interviews en allemand)
**Ce qui vous attend**
Vous occupez une **fonction stratégique** à forte dimension entrepreneuriale au sein d'une organisation solide et ambitieuse
Votre activité vous amène à vous déplacer dans toute la Suisse ; votre lieu de résidence est donc secondaire.
Vous évoluez à l'interface passionnante entre **conseil à la clientèle, Business Development, Case Management, assurances et gestion de la santé en entreprise.**

Business Developer / Junior FX Sales (m/w/d)
Ebury Hamburg – Präsenzstelle (100% In-Office)
Starte deine FinTech-Karriere als Business Developer / Junior FX Sales bei Ebury in unserem dynamischen Team in Hamburg!
Bist du bereit, deine Vertriebskarriere in der weltweiten FinTech-Branche zu starten und von einer ungedeckelten Provision zu profitieren? Bei uns erwartet dich kein kalter Sprung ins kalte Wasser, sondern eine zielgerichtete Einarbeitungsphase, persönliches Mentoring, echte Praxis und ein glasklarer Karrierepfad. Dein Ziel: Eine Top-Vertriebspersönlichkeit im Bereich Devisen (FX) und globale Zahlungsabwicklung zu werden.
Jedes Gespräch, das du führst, schärft deinen Sales-Instinkt und fördert deine persönliche Entwicklung. Du arbeitest mit modernsten Finanzlösungen, die Unternehmen beim globalen Handel unterstützen. Dabei baust du tiefgehendes Branchenwissen auf, das dir die Türen für zukünftige Führungspositionen öffnet.
Auf deinem Weg begleiten dich erfahrene Mentoren und strukturierte Entwicklungsprogramme, die deine Karriere auf das nächste Level katapultieren. Egal, ob du künftig ein eigenes Vertriebsteam leiten oder dich als Experte in der Bestandskundenbetreuung spezialisieren willst: Wir geben dir die Werkzeuge, das Know-how und den Boost, um deine ehrgeizigen Ziele zu erreichen.
Deine Aufgaben als Business Developer
Dealmaker & Networker: Aktive Akquise neuer Geschäftsmöglichkeiten durch gezielte Kontaktaufnahme mit Entscheidungsträgern (CEOs, CFOs) des deutschen Mittelstands (KMUs).
Marktanalyse & Pitching: Eigenständige Recherche von B2B-Kunden, Analyse der Finanzbedürfnisse im Auslandsgeschäft und maßgeschneiderte Präsentation unserer globalen Zahlungs- und Devisenlösungen.
Impact auf dein Gehalt: Präsentation, Verhandlung und Onboarding von B2B-Neukunden – je erfolgreicher dein Onboarding, desto höher deine Provision und dein Karriere-Speed.
Teamwork: Enger Austausch mit internen Fachabteilungen für ein nahtloses und schnelles Onboarding deiner Kunden.
Das bringst du mit
Deine Qualifikation: Du hast ein erfolgreich abgeschlossenes (Fach-)Hochschulstudium (z. B. BWL, VWL, Finance), eine kaufmännische Ausbildung (z. B. Bank, Außenhandel) oder möchtest als motivierter Quereinsteiger (mit B2B-Vertriebsvorerfahrung) mit Begeisterung für die Finanz- und Wirtschaftswelt durchstarten.
Sales-Drive: Erste Erfahrung im B2B-Sales/Vertrieb ist ein Pluspunkt, vor allem zählt aber deine echte Leidenschaft für den aktiven Kundenkontakt und deine Überzeugungskraft.
Keine FX-Vorerfahrung nötig: Wir setzen auf dein Potenzial und deine Persönlichkeit statt auf den „perfekten“ Lebenslauf. Unser Intensivprogramm der Ebury-BD-Academy bildet dich vom ersten Tag an umfassend aus.
Sprachkompetenz: Fließendes Deutsch sowie verhandlungssicheres Englisch für unser internationales Arbeitsumfeld.
Mindset: Kommunikationsstärke, intrinsische Motivation, Durchhaltevermögen und Bereitschaft, gesteckte Ziele nicht nur zu erreichen, sondern zu übertreffen.
Warum Ebury? Dein beschleunigter Karriereweg
Als eines der weltweit am schnellsten wachsenden FinTechs basiert unser Erfolg auf der gezielten Förderung junger Talente und transparenten Aufstiegschancen:
Weg 1 – Führungslaufbahn (Head of Desk): Entwickle dich vom Business Developer zum Sales Executive und sichere dir bei entsprechender Performance deine erste Beförderung bereits innerhalb der ersten 12 Monate .
Weg 2 – Expertenlaufbahn (Client Portfolio Manager): Übernahme und persönliche operative Betreuung von Finanzentscheidern und strategischen Bestandskunden.

Ungedeckelte Provision: Attraktives Grundgehalt kombiniert mit einem ungedeckelten Provisionsmodell, deine Leistung bestimmt dein Einkommen.
Fast-Track-Karriere: Ein transparentes, leistungsorientiertes Beförderungssystem ab Tag 1.
Ebury Business Developer Academy: Intensives Schulungs- und Bootcamp-Programm für deine Vertriebs- und Finanz-Skills.
1:1 Mentoring: Laufendes Coaching durch erfahrene Teamleiter und Senior Account Manager.
High-Energy-Kultur: Dynamisches, motivierendes und kollegiales Arbeitsumfeld mit starkem Fokus auf dein persönliches Wachstum.
Modernes Büro: Attraktive Büroräumlichkeiten in zentraler Lage in Hamburg.
Weitere Benefits: Umfangreiches Benefits-Paket (u. a. Wellhub/Gympass, Corporate Benefits, betriebliche Altersvorsorge (BAV), Pluxee-Card, regelmäßige Social Events & Promotion Bootcamps).
